name: lut_owner
description: demo.lut — the RESOURCE-HANDLE PATTERN demo lib plugin (docs/new_gen/14, appendix 'Resource-handle convention'). A TYPE-OWNER: heavy custom objects (an immutable sorted i64->i64 lookup table, the minimal honest build-once-query-many structure) never ride packs — this DLL constructs/destructs them and packs carry only the handle entry {type:'demo.lut', id, gen, $v} as a nested canonical-mp map. Ring of N slots with monotonic generation leases (a recycled slot's outstanding handles resolve to $fault stale_handle; generations are never reused, even across reinit); content-keyed build dedup (the zero-rebuild proof); demo.lut.dump is the byte-deterministic MATERIALIZER for persistence (handle entries are runtime-only).
_lib_doc: lib plugin marker (informational, doc 14): a capability provider, not a pipeline stage — do not wire it as an input/output of anything; create one instance and let consumers reach it by capability name through the host funnel.
_reentrant_doc: capability handlers are invoked by the host funnel WITHOUT per-instance serialization (the provider thread-safety contract); ring/dedup are mutex-guarded, resolve pins the object via shared_ptr so a concurrent recycle can never free it under a running query/dump, counters are atomics.
_on_fault_doc: a type owner whose handler faulted should stop serving (quarantine) rather than answer from possibly-corrupt state; every outstanding handle then fails closed at the funnel (-3), and a re-commit rebuild mints FRESH generations so pre-crash handles can only resolve stale, never alias.

params.name: ring_slots
params.doc: number of lease slots in the object ring; under pressure the LRU slot is recycled (its generation bumps and outstanding handles go stale). Shrinking recycles the dropped tail.

capabilities.name: demo.lut.build
capabilities.doc: Pack in: mp 'keys' (canonical array of i64), mp 'values' (array of i64, same length), i64 '$v' (opt, default 1) | bool '$probe'. Pack out: mp 'handle' {type:'demo.lut', id, gen, $v:1}, i64 'built' (1 = constructed now, 0 = content-dedup hit), i64 'builds' (lifetime — the zero-rebuild proof), i64 'size'. Contract failure -> $fault pack (missing_input/bad_input).

capabilities.name: demo.lut.query
capabilities.doc: Pack in: mp 'handle', mp 'keys' (array of i64), '$v'/'$probe' as above. Pack out: mp 'values' (i64 per found key, nil per missing), i64 'found', i64 'size', i64 'builds' (echo). Handle faults: wrong_type / stale_handle / bad_handle / unsupported_version.

capabilities.name: demo.lut.dump
capabilities.doc: Pack in: mp 'handle', '$v'/'$probe' as above. Pack out: bin 'lut' — the byte-deterministic canonical materialization ('XLUT' + u8 ver + be32 count + count*(be64 key, be64 value)), i64 'size', i64 'builds' (echo). Same handle faults as query. This is the persistence materializer: handle entries are runtime-only.

exchange.doc: -> {builds, dedup_hits, queries, dumps, recycles, stale_faults, wrong_type_faults, live, ring_slots, registered} — builds vs dedup_hits is the zero-rebuild proof counter
forced recycle of every live slot (generation bump; all outstanding handles go stale) -> {ok:true, recycled:N}
